questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 5 & 0 & 6 & 21\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-5{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+2z=0 \\  & y+2z=0 \\  & x+y+3z=1\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=6 \\  & y+z=5 \\  & 2x+3y+2z=14\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and hence solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 2 & 3 & 2 & 14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=-{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x+y+z=6 \\  & y+z=5 \\  & z=3,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=3$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y+(3)=5\,⟹\,y=5-3=2.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=2$ and $z=3$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x+(2)+(3)=6\,⟹\,x=6-5=1.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=1,y=2$ and $z=3.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by 

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -9 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ -2 & 5 & -4 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 3 & -5 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-2y+z=-3 \\  & y-2z=-2 \\  & z=8,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=8$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
y-2(8)=-2\,⟹\,y=-2+16=14.
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=14$ and $z=8$ into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(14)+(8)=-3\,⟹\,x=17.
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=17,y=14$, and $z=8.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨17,14,8⟩.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & x-y+2z=8 \\  & -2x+2y-3z=-11 \\  & x+z=9.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ -2 & 2 & -3 & -11 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 & 9\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 5\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+2z=8 \\ y-z=1 \\ z=5,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=5$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y-(5)=1\,⟹\,y=6.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=6$ and $z=5$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(6)+2(5)=8\,⟹\,x=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=4$, $y=6$, and $z=5.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}4 & -4 & -12 & 8 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 10 & -5 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{3}$ and the $3$rd row by $\frac{1}{7}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & -9 & -6 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 7 & -3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :=\frac{1}{7}{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -\frac{3}{7}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ -2 & -2 & 5 & -2 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 3 & 4 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 4\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x+y-2z=3 \\ y+5z=-8 \\ z=4,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=4$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+5(4)=-8\,⟹\,y=-28.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-28$ and $z=4$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x+(-28)-2(4)=3\,⟹\,x=39.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=39$, $y=-28$, and $z=4.$ Or, in vector form $⟨39,-28,4⟩.$

questions.problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ given by

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
questions.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -6 & 4 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 5 & -5 & 16 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-5){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 3 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 11\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, the system is now

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-y+3z=-2 \\ y+2z=-1 \\ z=11,\end{aligned}
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The third equation $z=11$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+2(11)=-1\,⟹\,y=-23.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, substituting $y=-23$ and $z=11$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-23)+3(11)=-2\,⟹\,x=-58.\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=-58$, $y=-23$, and $z=11.$ Or, in vector form, $⟨-58,-23,11⟩.$

questions.problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned} & 3x-6y+3z=-6 \\  & 2x-4y+3z=-1 \\  & 2y-4z=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
questions.worked_solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 & 3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{3}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 2 & -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Note that we get ${a}_{22}=0.$ Therefore, we swap the $2$nd and $3$rd rows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & ↔{R}_{3} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we multiply the $2$nd row by $\frac{1}{2}$ to get

$$
\begin{aligned} & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & -4 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -1 & 2 & 1 & -1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14072055/assets/dded05f0961034de6808d8f91f64afe8c367cec3c11fafdb26946090fa9c0891.png)

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $z=2$ tells us the value of $z.$ Substituting this value into the second equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y+(2)=-2\,⟹\,y=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting both $y=-4$ and $z=2$ into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x-(-4)+(2)=1\,⟹\,x=-5.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x=-5,$ $y=-4,$ and $z=2.$ Or, in vector form, $\langle -5,-4,2 \rangle.$
